newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa pumps first crude from offshore oil wells.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa pumps first crude from offshore oil wells.

text.p: After 20 years of searching for oil, South Africa said Monday it started pumping crude oil from offshore oil wells for the first time.
The "black gold" flowed out of the Oribi oilfield about 80 miles southwest of Mossel Bay at dawn and officials said they hoped to pump 20,000 barrels of crude a day.

The $75 million project, 80 percent state-owned and 20 percent owned by Energy Africa Ltd oil company, began production more than two months behind schedule, mainly because bad weather held up the refurbishment of the Orca production rig, the officials said.
South Africa has been converting gas found off Mossel Bay into gasoline for several years, but Monday's flow was the first commercial production of crude oil in the country's history.

The new production platform is expected to meet around 5 percent of South Africa's daily crude oil requirement. Sasol Ltd's oil-from-coal plants provide over 30 percent of the country's liquid fuel requirement.
The oil is being pumped into a 700,000-barrel tanker, which will take about a month to fill.
The first cargo will be ferried to the Caltex Oil SA refinery in Cape Town, which has agreed to take the oil field's initial 600,000 barrels. The second cargo will go to a refinery in Durban.

The Oribi oilfield output will taper off gradually over three to six years. It has probable recoverable reserves of 20 million barrels and will form the nucleus of the subsequent development of other oil finds in the area, which would extend production by another six years, officials said.
